correctness.rationale: For symmetric numerical semigroup S of multiplicity m≥4, reflection about Frobenius F identifies gaps f of H=S/3 with elements x=F−3f in residue r=F mod3; f is pseudo-Frobenius exactly when x is minimal under subtraction of positive S∩3Z. If r=0 then H is symmetric and PF(H)={F/3}. If r=1 or 2, any factorization of a source element in class r contains a generator of class r or a pair of generators of opposite class 3−r, so the residue module equals (G_r ∪ pair sums of G_{3−r}) + S0. Taking its minimal candidates c<F gives the exact PF list (F−c)/3 and the binomial generator-count bound. Apéry calculation for S=<m,m+d,...,m+(m−2)d> with 3|d and gcd(m,d)=1 gives PF(H)={d/3,...,(m−1)d/3} and type m−1, unboundedly sharp. Independent Apéry/member DP matches seven admissible parameter pairs. The universal claim rests on module duality and Apéry proof, not bounded enumeration.
